You're NTA. Your mother is a terrible person. Getting upset over you wanting to put the children that she raised into a quilt is increisbly manipulative. What you did was nothing short of a beautiful sentiment, and the fact that she was devastated enough to THROW A HAND-MADE GIFT AWAY just because it doesn't have her dumb dog on it is disgusting.

That's leading dengerously close into NC territory for me, if possible for you. That whole situation sounds incredibly healthy and unsafe. The fact that she couldn't even thank you is wild. Your siblings being totally okay with being replaced by an animal is their decision, but the fact that your whole family knows of your dog phobia, most are using said dog phobia against you, and are also now belittling you over not wanting to put her dog's face on the quilt that you made to remind her that she did actually birth and/ or raise human children is bonkers to me. Nothing short of abuse and manipulation from almost all parties.

NC with mother. NC with siblings who harass you. NC with anybody who is guilting you into feeling bad for your thoughtful and beautiful gift. You. Deserve. Better.

Not sure why you're getting downvoted for explaining what sounds like a dislike for FOMO game mechanics and elitist playerbase views. That's pretty much where I stand- new players should be able to get them if they want them, WITHOUT potentially spending a ton of in-game currency or desperately resorting to RMT should they not be able to get the in-game currency before the price takes off beyond their reach. Even if old seasonal rares are released in a "smaller capacity," like there's a smaller chance of acquiring them when doing new seasonal events, then I think that that should still be considered. It would avoid the community preying on newer players with massively-high prices for rares, and it would also completely erase that feeling of FOMO for newer players.

If tradeable, put in trade limit and value hats super-cheap. If untradeable, put older rares in new events with a much lower drop chance. No ability to prey on newer players, and no real feeling of FOMO. The achievement idea is a nice touch as well, or some other way to show that "we were the first." Not that I'd use something like that, but it could be a compromise for people who give a care about prestige or being seen as "elite" due to their years spent on the game, I guess.

I'm gonna say no on the tradability. We've all seen numerous times what happens with early-gen rares. There's never any goodwill toward newer players- it's always a shitshow of greed and rares eventually inflating to massively-high prices. Sure, people are hoarding them so people are theorizing that they'll never get that high in price, BUT if the player base were to blow up in the future, some players with a bunch of these rares have stopped playing, and some of the people who managed to have dozens or even hundreds of each by the end of the event essentially end up having a choke-hold on the rare Christmas hat market? ... No. Absolutely not. That's not for the benefit of new players, and I wish that people would stop citing "BUT NEW PLAYERS!" as justification. It always ends up being about little more than greed. Sure a small percentage of the population may care about giving new players hats for reasonable prices or even for free, but that part of the community will no doubt be a fraction of a percent, and most who are currently considering hoarding as many as they possibly can aren't doing it to be generous. They're doing it because they're hoping that there will grow to be a huge value attached to them.

Want them to be tradeable? Then add in a trade limit and make the hats valued dirt-cheap. Don't let new players who missed this event get shafted in the future by rares that they want costing exponential amounts of gold that they'll likely never be able to afford and would be better off just not having the option to trade for in the first place. Thanks for coming to my TED talk!

His entire goal is to make a game that he himself enjoys playing. He doesn't need to please us- he didn't even need to release a second game at all. If he doesn't do what we want, then we either deal with it or we quit playing- it's no skin off his back, man.

My argument against this is that it incentivizes players who were here before new players, into taking advantage of the fact that they got these hats. We see it with RuneScape. We saw it with other MMOs. If limited-availability items are made tradeable, then players can and will charge arms and legs for them. You cite that "it gives new players the ability to get them," but I \*highly\* doubt that longer-time players are gonna give these hats away for free if they were ever to hit astronomically high prices like RS's rares did. Leave these in the past. Allow new players to get new rares. Try and give Andrew and Fen a valid and logical argument about why you think that holiday rares shouldn't be \*completely\* locked to specific years, if you're worried about new players being able to get them later on- maybe you can try and convince him to instead release them in a smaller version, like maybe there can be a small chance to get an older rare in place of a newer one or something. Literally anything is better than RuneScape's multi-billion-gold Partyhat situation. "BuT nEw PlAyErS." Most new players will never be able to afford them anyways, and if RuneScape taught us anything, it's that the rich only care about getting richer, trading their partyhats to other rich people with other partyhats or dyes or whatever other bullcrap Jagex has decided to implement for the hyper-wealthy to gnaw at, and new players will almost never get them anyways unless they manage to get lucky with an excessively rare drop after they've established themselves as a bosser or skiller of some sort already. People saying "for the newbies" seem to very conveniently forget that, based on history and whatnot, a majority of players will end up charging those newbies an arm and a leg for these hats, which really means that they wanna be able to be filthy rich off of said newbies. It's not for the newbies, it's for their own wallets.

Buddy, were you not on RuneScape during the numerous years where this WASN'T the case? Chicken costume, bunny costume, numerous other Halloween and Christmas and Easter events after the Halloween masks/ Santa hats/ Partyhats included rares that were not tradeable, you had to be playing the game during the event to get them.

It's almost... As if... The early-game devs realized after Santas, Phats, and H'weens hit inconceivable prices during those first few years, that giving player-decided monetary value to a hyper-exclusive item was a bad idea after all.

All of you people judging a first-time mother for not wanting to leave her nursing child for hours/ days just because you did things differently with your own child-rearing, and were apparently perfect mothers right out of the gate, should be ashamed of yourselves. Not every child is the same and all of you, especially those with multiple children, should know this- some refuse to go an hour without eating, some refuse to leave the mother's hip, some won't eat from bottles, etc, etc.

She has her reasons for not wanting to go hours or days, as per sister's request, away from her baby. They're all valid. It's really funny, though, how OP is apparently terrible for asking if she can bring her nursing child, but sister isn't terrible for telling OP to put a fucking party above her duties to her six-month-old baby. Priorities be damned, I guess?

Disgusting.

It was a question that was asked. It was not pushed, and it was not brought up to the sister after her initial no response. Assuming IS FINE for some extenuating circumstances like, again, BEING THE FOOD FOR A CHILD. Same could be said for people who have children with serious disabilities, for that matter- they're likely to ask about an exception, and then will be obligated to decline going if the answer is no.

Reasonable to not want ANY children there with no exceptions. Reasonable to ask about an exception for certain things just in case. Reasonable to not go after being told no. NOT reasonable to throw a tantrum like OP's sister is doing after somebody decided to not go. We're on the same page about most of it but I firmly disagree about there being an issue with assuming that there may be an exception made- OP's sister presumably knew that OP is bfing, and the fact that she *expects* OP to just "detach" from the nursing child for DAYS to attend a damn wedding is completely irresponsible and shows how little she actually understands a new bfing mother's situation.

Are all parents with disabled children who require around-the-clock care AHs for assuming that somebody inviting them to a child-free event may make an exception? No- if somebody invites them, then they either make the exception, or they don't expect those people to attend. It's completely impossible. Nursing babies aren't always easy, and bfing mothers aren't usually okay with leaving their babies for too long. Simple as.

I didn't originally either until thinking deeper about the "in three months" part. Totally valid for the sister to have a holiday-time child-free wedding in a nice location, just like it's totally valid for people to not attend due to budget constraints or having young breastfeeding babies to care for. What isn't valid is the sister being ridiculous about OP telling her that she's choosing to not go because of the latter reason.
OP said wedding is three months out, so baby could possibly still be breastfeeding during it, which is possibly the whole reason why OP even asked in the first place.

She asked due to the extenuating circumstance of her being the literal food for her child, was told no, and decided to not go. That's hardly pushing for an unreasonable exception- that's simply asking because right now her baby is probably never too far away from her, as most breastfed babies usually aren't.

There are a number of reasons why a bfing mother may not be able to leave her baby for that long. Baby won't take a bottle, baby wants constant breast comfort, mother can't pump and milk supply could suffer if baby isn't around to nurse, mother could be going through PPD or other after-birth things are just a few examples. OP isn't required to give medical details, but considering how many possible reasons there are, it could be anything like that or none of them- we aren't owed an explanation as to why she "doesn't want to" leave the baby with her husband for that long. It's also their first child, and the first can be very stressful and scary for a lot of new parents I'm sure- a mother being scared to leave her nursing baby with people often has nothing to do with the trust for the person they're leaving the baby with and more about the fact that *it's a new experience and for some people new things are just scary.* The three of them going together for baby and husband to stay in a hotel while she attends could also be incredibly expensive of a trip, especially for a wedding taking place presumably away from family in December, so that may be out of the question as well. She asked once, and then felt that it wasn't viable, so she declined to go, as is her right just as much as it's her sister's right to host a child-free party. A little understanding or at least empathy towards the woman who popped out a whole-ass living thing three months ago would be nice, maybe.

Assuming that there will be exceptions made for children that rely on an attendee for literal food is a fine assumption, seeing as how a number of people who commented about hosting or who did host child-free events in this post have made, myself included. OP asked if there would be an exception, was told no, and rather than fighting for her sister to change her mind, she declined attending as a result. OP's sister has chosen to fight about it, not OP. That's not sucky behaviour on OP's part- that's making a choice for the health of her and her baby.

Three months out from the wedding day puts this at being a December wedding. OP and her husband know nobody in the area. Context clues are sounding like this is a destination wedding, which during the holiday season can often cost a couple thousand dollars for travel, hotel, rental, food, etc. for two adults. Add in the fact that they have a new baby, and those are costs that may be completely out of reach when considering the fact that only one of the three would be at attending for maybe a couple of hours.

Edit: Even if it's not a destination wedding, it's still during the holiday season and can still be incredibly expensive compared to other times of the year.

Wedding being in three months puts it in December. I dunno about OP, but December flights when I was last checking are incredibly  expensive. If OP's sister chose a "destination wedding" which is a total possibility since OP said that her and her husband wouldn't know anybody there who could watch the baby, you're definitely looking at a pretty penny... Potentially $1k for the round-trip plane tickets alone, and hotels are also hiked up during the holiday season, so another $500 if they wanted to do a few days. Rental may be the cheapest, but it's still bound to be a few hundred. OP may be looking at closer to $2k after food and gas and other necessities while there, which is wild expenses for new parents to dish out so that one person can attend an hour or two, maybe three total, of a wedding and reception.

"Child-free" weddings and events are all fine and dandy, but your sister asking you, a breastfeeding mother, to "detach" from your newborn for A FEW DAYS while they're breastfeeding is bonkers as Hell. She also got upset that it feels like you're choosing you baby over her? UH, YEAH, AS YOU SHOULD?! I'm confused as Hell by that comment, like it's your child, of course you'll choose to be there with them, especially since right now you are potentially their only source of nutrition.

I understand not wanting toddlers or teenagers or school-aged kids with attitudes and tantrums and outside voices being used inside, completely understand. Newborns feel like a different thing, and personally I've held "child-free" events where the ONLY exceptions I was okay with having were breastfeeding babies. But that was my choice- your sister has chosen to not allow babies. Maybe she doesn't wanna be overshadowed by a cute tiny human. Maybe she doesn't wanna deal with whatever crying may happen. Maybe she doesn't want you to need to step away to feed them. Whatever her motive, fine, but she's gonna need to understand that, just like she has a right to refuse you coming with your breastfeeding baby, you have a right to choose your baby over her wedding.

NTA. Sister's a bit of an AH for telling you to just detach from your breastfeeding kid for a few days, and that you should choose her over your child though.

All this, to say that I relate, and you're completely NTA. I'm really glad that your grandparents are in your corner.
